item.title: Why the WHO must declare climate change a public health emergency
item.description: Across the world, people have felt the impacts of climate change firsthand. The Northern Hemisphere has had another record-breaking summer season of heat and extreme weather events. item.title: Islands harbor nearly 20% of Earth's biodiversity, yet remain overlooked in conservation strategies
item.description: Although they account for just 7% of the Earth's land surface, island ecosystems harbor almost 20% of the world's biodiversity. From sea-level rise to biological invasions, islands are facing multiple pressures associated with ongoing global change, and yet they are still overlooked in global biodiversity conservation strategies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why I sent my archive of nature’s sounds to France (commentary)
item.description: It is a peculiar irony: as technology reaches ever deeper into Earth’s living systems, the primal sonic expressions of the natural world—wind, water, leaf, and creature—have never been more imperiled. Soundscape ecology rests on a simple conviction: the collective voices of the nonhuman world are not only eloquent, but essential. Recorded and preserved over time, […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: US public lands tracker highlights the collective impact of Trump policies
item.description: In his second term as the U.S. president, Donald Trump has taken actions to remove protections from at least 34.8 million hectares (86 million acres) of public lands, according to the advocacy group Center for American Progress. The nonprofit Conservation Lands Foundation (CLF) recently catalogued 12 such policy actions in its newly released Public Lands […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Cyclone batters India’s eastern coast, killing 3 and damaging homes and farmland
item.description: KAKINADA, India (AP) — A powerful cyclone battered India ’s Andhra Pradesh state on Wednesday, killing at least three people and damaging homes and farmland after authorities evacuated tens of thousands of people, officials said. Cyclone Arnab made landfall early Wednesday as a very severe cyclonic storm before weakening to a severe cyclonic storm as […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Britain's King Charles III attends youth rally in the Bahamas
item.description: Britain’s King Charles III on Tuesday addressed a youth gathering at Clifford Park in Nassau, recalling the Bahamas’ independence celebrations in 1973 and highlighting the country’s cultural achievements and vulnerability to climate change. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: Urban street trees lose much of their capacity to cool during droughts
item.description: The combination of heat waves and drought markedly reduces the capacity of street trees to cool the air in Mediterranean cities. The lack of soil moisture severely restricts plant transpiration, reducing the thermal relief provided by these trees during extreme heat events. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Just Helping recycled 88,544 Xmas trees in 2026 and raised a record £1,885,915 for local UK causes
item.description: A charitable organization in the UK has triumphantly gathered 88,544 discarded Christmas trees, turning them into valuable products. This initiative raised £1.88 million for various local charities, breaking past records. The substantial involvement of volunteers during the collection phase contributed greatly, while the campaign fostered significant environmental progress by curbing carbon emissions. The charity envisions expanding its recycling efforts to cover more regions in the future. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Since 2022, workers have turned an illegal dump in FDR Park into a 33-acre wetland with 7,000 trees
item.description: In South Philadelphia, a once-neglected dumping ground has been reborn as a thriving tidal wetland, nurturing local wildlife. This impressive restoration project earned the Governor’s Award for Environmental Excellence from Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection. Not only does it serve as a crucial natural flood management system for stormwater, but it also enhances biodiversity by drawing in a variety of birds and mammals. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: As wildfires rage, Canadian researchers study the life that comes after
item.description: The reporting and photography for this story was fully supported by a 2025-2026 grant from the Sitka Foundation and the Science Media Centre of Canada. Four of the five worst years recorded for global forest fires occurred since 2021. And 2026 is no exception, with hundreds of thousands in North America, Europe and Africa forced […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: A rare hound with a storied past faces an uncertain future in Bangladesh
item.description: Dogs are generally not treated well in Bangladesh, where the majority Muslim population holds a conservative approach to domesticating dogs. Here, kicking a resting or passing stray dog is often seen as amusing. This hostile attitude, for decades, justified the authorities culling stray dogs. In 2019, the passing of the Animal Welfare Act finally put […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: ‘A proper seat at the table’: Lucy Mulenkei on Indigenous decision-making at the COP17 biodiversity summit
item.description: YEREVAN, Armenia — Two years ago at the 2024 U.N. biodiversity conference (COP 16) in Cali, Colombia, a meeting room packed with people representing some of the world’s thousands of Indigenous Peoples, erupted into cheering and applause. After three decades of hard work and negotiations, a seemingly obscure group within the Convention on Biological Diversity […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: A single sauna session sends immune cells surging through your body
item.description: A new Finnish study reveals that just 30 minutes in a sauna can temporarily flood the bloodstream with additional white blood cells, potentially helping the immune system patrol the body and detect threats. The surprising response resembles the immune boost seen during exercise and may help explain some of the health benefits linked to sauna bathing. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Livelihood, education goals affect migration under climate change
item.description: Climate-driven hazards can push many to leave their homes in search of a livelihood elsewhere, but aspirations for the future may change where they decide to migrate, according to a new study led by researchers at Penn State. At the same time, income losses due to climate shocks, or extreme weather events like floods or droughts, may constrain migration options for vulnerable populations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Will it be AI or the climate crisis that ends humanity? We can make it neither | Adam McKay and Philip Eubanks
item.description: Both of these threats have the same roots: private entities seeking to cash in. We have the power to stand against them A summer of extreme heat, entire villages obliterated in Nepal, a super El Niño breaking records, Exxon publicly saying we may reach 3C by 2050 – could it possibly be any worse? How about throwing AI extinction in the mix? Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Adam McKay and Philip Eubanks

item.title: Record heat-related deaths in 2023, WHO-partnered report finds
item.description: Climate inaction continues to harm and kill people in all countries with a record 710,000 estimated deaths globally from heat in 2023, a UN-partnered report warned on Wednesday. For the first time, more than seven in 10 fatalities were attributable to human-caused climate change. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Ocean’s ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
item.description: The ocean absorbs around 30 per cent of human-caused carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and 90 per cent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases. But climate change has already reduced its capacity to absorb carbon by approximately six per cent, a new UN report warns ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
item.description: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Cambio climático: En 2023, el calor mató a 700.000 personas
item.description: La falta de coraje para afrontar la crisis climática sigue dañando y matando a personas en todos los países, con un récord estimado de 710.000 muertes globales por calor en 2023, advirtió este miércoles un informe con colaboración de la ONU. Por primera vez, más de siete de cada diez fallecimientos fueron atribuibles al cambio climático causado por el hombre. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Families brace for a fourth winter of wind, rain and floods in Gaza’s camps
item.description: Gaza's impending winter is likely to lead to further devastation for Palestinians. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: This flower smells like rotting flesh
item.description: Meet the Rhizanthes lowii, a rare parasitic flowering plant that has evolved its stink to attracting flies that help pollinate the flower. It blooms for only a few days, and is found in the jungles of Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo—which are home to some of the strangest plants on Earth. Join Conservation Entangled host Izzy on […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: The climate crisis will destroy our economies – we learned this 20 years ago. When will we act? | Fiona Harvey
item.description: The radical Stern report showed that a low-carbon future is also good economics. But it seems that capitalism needs a reminder Saving the only planet we have makes good economic sense. There is, after all, no money to be made on a dead Earth. There may be costs involved now, but they are worth paying to protect our children from certain destruction. These propositions seem self-evident now. But two decades ago, mainstream economists had very different ideas. They had proved that the climate crisis would be a mere economic blip, easily absorbed by growing economies and therefore not worth… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: As the sea swallows a Nigerian community, migratory bird habitat disappears
item.description: The point where land meets sea at Ayetoro, in southwestern Nigeria, is marked by the skeletons of now-submerged landmarks. Birdcalls, crashing waves, and the sounds of local fishing boats’ outboard engines wash over the crumbling remains of old buildings as well as a wetland that’s a vital stopover and wintering site for migratory waterbirds like […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Pangolin scale lawsuit in Indonesia could shake up how wildlife traffickers pay
item.description: When customs officials at Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok Port opened a shipping container flagged for inspection in February 2026, they expected to find sea cucumbers and instant noodles as indicated on the consignment paperwork. Instead, they found 3,053 kilograms (6,730 pounds) of dried pangolin scales destined for Cambodia. It was among Indonesia’s largest seizures of the […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Sea of crimson: vivid ‘red beach’ transforms China’s wetlands and marshes – in pictures
item.description: A striking transformation takes place along the coast of Qingdao in autumn, when a native seepweed turns a brilliant shade of red. The ‘red beach’ phenomenon can be seen in the salt marshes and wetlands on the coast of China’s Shandong province, where the Suaeda glauca plant matures and absorbs water, changing it from green to crimson between September and November Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Guardian Staff

item.title: Scientists collected DNA from seawater at 316 sites across Japan;126 fish species farther north
item.description: Japan is witnessing a dramatic transformation in its marine ecosystems as rising ocean temperatures prompt fish species to migrate northward. An extensive research effort involving the analysis of water samples has revealed profound implications for local fisheries, economies, and the overall health of marine life. With the introduction of new species, traditional fishing methods may need to evolve, underscoring the crucial role of environmental DNA in monitoring these biodiversity changes. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: London homeowner ordered to repay £225,000 to Thames Water over flood claim
item.description: London resident Karen Imber faced legal action after claiming her flood-affected home was unsellable during mediation. Claiming damages from sewage flooding, she settled for £225,000. However, unbeknownst to the mediators, Imber had already sold the property for £780,000 prior. Thames Water uncovered the sale, leading to a court ruling that required her to return the settlement funds, highlighting issues of fraudulent misrepresentation. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Artificial nests help Hong Kong’s rare cockatoos cope with a ‘housing crisis’
item.description: In the urban landscape of Hong Kong, artificial nest boxes are providing shelter and research opportunities for one of the world’s most threatened parrot species. The yellow-crested cockatoo (Cacatua sulphurea) is critically endangered, with fewer than 2,000 individuals remaining across its native range in eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste. However, Hong Kong hosts roughly 200 wild […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: A Thai rescue center gives injured leopard cat cubs a second chance
item.description: At a government wildlife rescue center in Thailand, dozens of lost and injured baby leopard cats are receiving a second chance at life in the wild. Annual admission of leopard cats (Prionailurus bengalensis) at the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation rescue center in Khon Kaen, in northeastern Thailand, have surged from an […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Island Recovery After Eradication: Native forests regrow on Nu’utele; turtles and rare birds return
item.description: Nu’utele Island in Samoa is witnessing a remarkable revival as invasive rats and pigs have been eradicated. This positive shift has encouraged the resurgence of native bird species and provided safe nesting grounds for sea turtles. Furthermore, local communities are experiencing enhanced food production linked to the restoration of native plants. Such revitalization underscores the critical need for ongoing conservation efforts to safeguard biodiversity and combat climate change effects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Photographer Tom Hegen’s aerial eye reveals the true scale of the critical mineral age
item.description: From the air, the vivid lithium fields of Chile’s Atacama Desert look like an intricate computer circuit board, hinting at the technological destination of this increasingly crucial mineral. Photographer Tom Hegen has spent the past six years documenting some of the world’s most significant mining regions that supply the critical minerals needed for modern technologies […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Over 1,000 still in Japan shelters 3 months after Kumamoto quake: ‘exhausted all the time’
item.description: More than 1,000 people are still taking shelter in evacuation centres, awaiting temporary housing three months after a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Japan’s Kumamoto prefecture, damaging their homes. The quake occurred at 4.27pm on July 28. As of Monday, the death toll stood at 38 – 36 from confirmed disaster-related causes and two suspected to be disaster-related – bringing the number of casualties to 420. Evacuation centres remain open at 21 locations in seven cities and towns. In... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Report indicates water, food and power at risk by strong El Niño
item.description: Rainfall reductions of up to 80% and torrential precipitation leading to severe flooding and landslides are the expected consequences across different areas of Latin America and the Caribbean from the impact of the El Niño phenomenon in 2027, according to a report co-authored by the General Secretariat of the Organization of American States (OAS), which urges member states to strengthen prevention and preparedness during the final months of 2026. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate health harms outpace action, prompting calls for global health emergency
item.description: The 2026 Report of The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change finds that many of the health risks and harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement was introduced (2016–2025) than in the decade before it (2006–2015). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Plan for multibillion-pound Sizewell nuclear plant a ‘terrible deal’ for UK taxpayers, MPs say
item.description: The public accounts committee has said the risk to billpayers is ‘extraordinary’ The government’s plan to fund a multibillion-pound nuclear plant at the Sizewell site in Suffolk represents a “terrible deal” for the UK taxpayer over the rest of the century, according to the government’s spending watchdog. MPs on the public accounts committee (PAC) have warned the government that the cost of the Sizewell C nuclear reactor could spiral to almost £48bn, leaving bill payers on the hook to provide an extra £9.8bn to construct the plant before 2040 and a further £12bn over its 60-year operating… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Decoding the loopy physics of hula hooping with high-tech earthquake sensors
item.description: Hula hooping may be literal child's play, but as it turns out, the physics behind the gym-class staple is so complicated that scientists have spent decades trying to understand how the hula hoop defies gravity. Fuente: Phys.org.
